summary:
Astronaut Health Monitor is a web app that lets a mission team check the health of an entire space crew on one screen. At its centre is an interactive human body. A beating heart and breathing lungs follow each astronaut’s live heart rate and respiration, and tapping any organ opens its readings, a trend chart and a plain-language explanation. The app also shows a live ECG, cabin conditions such as CO2, pressure, oxygen and radiation, and slower risks like bone loss, muscle loss, sleep and radiation dose.

It addresses the challenge by turning many separate measurements into simple Normal, Watch and Critical statuses, and by logging an alert the moment a reading leaves its safe range. Reading body data next to cabin data helps the team tell whether a problem comes from the person or the environment. Everything runs in a browser, even offline.

This matters because missions to the Moon and Mars will be far from Earth, with delayed communication. Microgravity strains the heart, bones, muscles and sleep, and these effects grow on long trips. Clear, fast health information supports earlier action and safer decisions. The prototype uses simulated data and can be connected to real sensors.
details:
ASTRA – Astronaut Health with NOVA AI

Project Overview

ASTRA is an AI-powered astronaut healthcare and wellbeing application designed to support astronauts before, during, and after space missions. It provides a centralized platform to monitor health information, manage daily wellbeing, access medical guidance, and support post-mission recovery.

The application includes NOVA (Neural Operations and Vitality Assistant), an AI-powered companion that helps astronauts interact with the system, understand health information, receive wellbeing guidance, and access relevant assistance.

How It Works

ASTRA organizes astronaut healthcare into different modules, including:

  • Health Monitoring: Displays health information, vital trends, and personal health records.
  • Space Adaptation: Supports astronauts in understanding and managing the challenges of adapting to space environments.
  • Mental Wellbeing: Provides mood tracking, daily check-ins, and wellbeing support.
  • Cognitive Support: Includes features related to cognitive health and mental performance.
  • Medication and Nutrition: Helps organize medication schedules and nutrition-related information.
  • Medical Connect: Supports consultation summaries and medical follow-up tracking.
  • Emergency Support: Provides emergency guidance, safety information, and event logging.
  • Post-Mission Recovery: Supports rehabilitation and recovery tracking after returning to Earth.
  • NOVA AI Assistant: Provides conversational assistance and access to relevant application information.

NOVA uses Groq Cloud AI for AI-powered conversations. When cloud AI is unavailable, it can switch to an offline knowledge base and rule-based responses.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA aims to make astronaut healthcare more organized, accessible, and supportive throughout space missions.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Helping astronauts keep track of their health and wellbeing.
  • Supporting early awareness of changes in health trends.
  • Making health information easier to understand through an AI assistant.
  • Providing access to basic guidance when cloud connectivity is unavailable.
  • Supporting mental wellbeing and daily health check-ins.
  • Improving organization of medical information and post-mission recovery activities.

The long-term goal is to contribute to safer, more informed, and more astronaut-centred healthcare during space exploration.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using:

  • React and TypeScript for the application interface and functionality.
  • Vite for development and building.
  • Tailwind CSS for styling and responsive design.
  • Groq Cloud AI API with the GPT-OSS-20B model for NOVA's AI functionality.
  • Dexie.js and IndexedDB for local offline data storage.
  • Three.js for 3D visual elements.
  • Recharts for data visualization.
  • Web Speech API for voice input and speech functionality.
  • Render for application hosting.
  • ChatGPT and Grok for AI-assisted brainstorming, coding, debugging, and development.

Creativity and Innovation

The main creative feature of ASTRA is the integration of NOVA, an AI companion, into a complete astronaut healthcare platform rather than treating the AI assistant as a separate chatbot.

The application combines health monitoring, wellbeing support, medical organization, emergency guidance, and recovery features in one interface. Its offline-first approach allows important application functions to remain available even when cloud connectivity is unavailable.

It also includes accessibility options, multilingual support, privacy controls, and clear identification of simulated health data.

Factors Considered During Development

The project was designed with the following factors in mind:

  1. Astronaut Safety: Health guidance should be cautious and should not replace qualified medical professionals.
  2. Privacy: Personal health information should remain under the astronaut's control.
  3. Connectivity: Offline functionality is important when internet access is limited.
  4. Accessibility: The interface should support different screen sizes, themes, and text sizes.
  5. Data Reliability: Simulated information should be clearly distinguished from actual measured health data.
  6. Usability: Health information and important functions should be easy to understand and access.

ASTRA is currently a prototype using simulated demonstration data. It is not connected to real medical sensors or operational spacecraft medical systems.
